corrections.exactBefore: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.
corrections.after: I have dwelt in your country a long time, and I am loath to kill you.
corrections.sourceReason: 恨不殺汝 here expresses reluctance to kill the pursuers; the ZZTJ 96 parallel reads 吾居汝國久恨恨，不欲殺汝. The current English reverses the sense into a wish to have killed them.

corrections.exactBefore: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”
corrections.after: I never expected that this resolve would go unfulfilled; I die with lingering regret. It is fate. What can be done!
corrections.sourceReason: The current English drops 不圖 (did not expect) and 沒有餘恨 (die with lingering regret) and turns 命也奈何 into a flat statement.
